notes: Sleep was already disabled on this laptop (AC and DC), so no power setting was changed.
Draft stills render in about 2 s, full-resolution preview (128 samples) in about 20 s on the RTX 4060; the first render after a cold start spends about 75 s loading kernels.
While the camera is parked, src/comp/composite.py takes everything outside the wet part of the tank from the filmed plate.

Renders needed per scape (python src/comp/assemble.py --needs): 01 606-967, 02 952-1282, 03 1267-1597, 04 1582-1912, 05 1897-2309. Sequence render: blender -b --python src/blender/build.py -- --scape ID --frames A-B --outdir <work>/renders/ID --quality final.
When several Blender renders share the GPU, set AQUARIUM_CPU_DENOISE=1 to avoid OIDN out-of-memory errors.
Lamp is ten spot LEDs totalling 50 W by default; scapes override via LIGHT/WATER dicts (see src/blender/README.md).
Scapes 02 and 03 were briefed before fish.School existed: convert them from fish.shoal to SCAPE + fish.School + animate(ctx, frame) like scape 01, and add shrimp/snail where their briefs left TODOs.

Polish to do before final render: match the rendered glass edge colour to the filmed pale cyan (EDGE_GLOW and absorption in src/blender/tank.py) so the hand-over at frame 700 does not shift the edge strips; verify caustics are visible on sand and stone in motion.

Root cause worth remembering: any object a scape creates must be a Cycles caustics receiver or it gets no lamp light through the water. build.py now marks every object created after the base scene, including scatter sources.
Never run two Blender renders at once on this machine (16 GB RAM): it triggered a low-memory stop of all background jobs. Subagents rendering in parallel count too.

Renders take a machine-wide lock (build.render_lock), so renders started side by side queue instead of overlapping. Still never start a long sequence render while subagents are iterating on stills: it would hold the lock for its whole run.

The shoal is one simulation for the whole film. Any change to any scape's SWIM, or to the timeline, changes the fish's path from that point on. Settle all SWIMs before the final render and never mix frames rendered before and after such a change.

Film is now ten scapes, 3450 frames (115 s), about 3260 frames to render. At final quality that is roughly double the earlier estimate; time one final frame per scape before starting and tell the owner the total.
Never send two render commands in the same message: they interleave under the render lock and each call can outlast its timeout. One render command at a time, in sequence.

Heartbeat: session cron job, every 30 minutes while work can move; every 3 hours while everything waits on the owner. Session-only; recreate it if the session restarts (CronList shows the current id).
